Apple's autumn iPhone launch event is expected to be different this year. Rumours suggest that instead of the usual four similarly designed models, the September lineup will focus on flagship devices, including three high-end models: the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone 18 Pro Max, and what is widely expected to be called the iPhone Ultra — Apple's first foldable phone.

Among the three high-end iPhone options, which one would you choose?

If you prefer a traditional design, according to rumours, the iPhone 18 Pro will feature a smaller Dynamic Island, a 2nm-process A20 Pro chip, Apple's in-house C2 modem, longer battery life, and a significantly upgraded camera system. The larger-screened Pro Max is expected to retain the traditional iPhone design with a triple-lens camera system while packing a notably larger battery.

The rumoured iPhone Ultra is the most groundbreaking option this year: a book-style foldable design with an approximately 5.5-inch outer display and a 7.8-inch inner display, a slim titanium body, Touch ID replacing Face ID, and only two rear cameras. Reports suggest the display will be crease-free and will feature the A20 Pro chip, but the starting price is expected to be around US$2,000 or more.

If these rumours turn out to be true, which new iPhone are you planning to buy? Feel free to cast your vote and share your thoughts and reasons in the comments section!
